questions.question: What is a mosaic?
choices: An image or pattern assembled from small pieces of material
A drawing made only with charcoal
A sculpture carved from one stone
A printed book page

questions.question: Byzantine mosaics often use gold backgrounds. What effect can this create?
choices: A realistic outdoor landscape
A luminous, otherworldly setting that emphasizes spiritual presence
A measurement of natural sunlight
A system of linear perspective

questions.question: What was an icon in Byzantine art?
choices: A secular map of trade routes
A type of Gothic arch
A devotional image, often of Christ, Mary, or a saint
A royal tax record

questions.question: Why were religious images important in many medieval communities?
choices: They replaced all oral traditions
They were produced only as private decoration
They were forbidden in every church
They supported worship, teaching, devotion, and shared religious identity

questions.question: What is an illuminated manuscript?
choices: A handwritten book decorated with painted images and ornament
A stone building lit by candles
A printed newspaper
A musical instrument

questions.question: In an illuminated manuscript, gold leaf and vivid color could
choices: prove the text was printed by machine
mark important passages and enhance the book's visual and devotional value
create a photographic record
serve as a map scale

questions.question: Which architectural feature is strongly associated with Gothic cathedrals?
choices: Doric columns only
Concrete domes only
Pointed arches
Steel trusses

questions.question: How did stained glass contribute to many Gothic church interiors?
choices: It supported the building's foundation alone
It replaced all sculpture
It created a flat, unlit wall
It admitted colored light and presented religious narratives or symbols

questions.question: What is a flying buttress?
choices: An exterior support that helps transfer the thrust of a high wall or vault
A decorative manuscript border
A type of mosaic tile
A free-standing altar

questions.question: Compared with many Gothic churches, Romanesque churches often have
choices: glass curtain walls and steel frames
thick walls, rounded arches, and relatively small windows
pointed arches and extensive flying buttresses only
no stone construction

questions.question: Why might a medieval church commission an altarpiece?
choices: To replace the church's entire liturgy
To measure the building's height
To focus devotion and communicate sacred stories in a worship space
To record the daily weather

questions.question: Many medieval images use a hierarchical scale. What does that mean?
choices: All figures are drawn to measured natural size
Figures are placed only by distance
Every image uses one vanishing point
More important figures may be shown larger than less important ones

questions.question: What is one reason artists used symbolic attributes with saints?
choices: The objects helped viewers identify the figures and their stories
The objects recorded the artist's signature only
The symbols prevented any religious interpretation
The objects showed exact geographic scale

questions.question: Why are many Byzantine figures shown frontally and with solemn expressions?
choices: The artists could not draw profiles
The pose can convey authority, devotion, and a timeless sacred presence
The figures were always portraits from life
The style was designed to imitate photography

questions.question: What did guilds often contribute to medieval art production?
choices: A ban on apprenticeships
A system of digital image editing
Training, standards, and organization for craftspeople and workshops
The invention of oil paint in every region

questions.question: A cathedral's sculpted portal depicts biblical scenes. What could this communicate to visitors?
choices: A private household budget
A sequence of royal elections
A scientific diagram of anatomy
Religious narratives and ideas at a prominent entrance

questions.question: What does the term 'iconoclasm' refer to in historical discussions of Byzantine images?
choices: Disputes or actions concerning the use or destruction of religious images
A method of mixing fresco pigment
A type of cathedral vault
A manuscript binding technique

questions.question: Why should a viewer distinguish an original medieval work from a later restoration?
choices: Restored works have no historical value
Restoration choices can affect what is visible and how the work is interpreted
Every restoration recreates the original exactly
Only the frame can be changed

questions.question: Which feature best helps identify a Gothic cathedral interior?
choices: Low ceilings and flat roofs only
A circular Roman amphitheater
Tall vertical spaces with pointed arches and ribbed vaults
A timber house with no openings

questions.question: When comparing medieval and Byzantine art, what is a useful question?
choices: Which artwork is objectively the most beautiful?
Which artist used the newest digital tool?
Which work has the largest canvas?
How do materials, religious purposes, and regional traditions shape the visual choices?
